title: Umm Ma'bad's goat
hookLine: the sirah tells of a thin goat in a woman's tent giving milk when he touched it

cards: Dust, heat, and a tent on the road north. The travelers are hungry. They stop at the tent of a woman the sirah calls Umm Ma'bad, known for giving food and water to people passing by.
They ask if she has meat or dates to sell. She has nothing. It's been a hard, dry season, and the flock is out grazing.
All that's left at the tent is one goat, too thin and weak to go out with the others. This story isn't from Bukhari or Muslim; it comes from the sirah and other collections. Today: Umm Ma'bad.

teach.h: IF YOU SEE MILK IN HER, MILK HER.
teach.b: In the story, the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, notices the goat at the side of the tent and asks Umm Ma'bad about it. Too weak to go with the flock, she says. Does the goat have any milk?

Far too worn out for that. He asks her permission to milk her anyway, and her answer is lovely: if you see milk in her, then milk her. He rubs the goat's udder, says the name of Allah, and prays, and the milk comes.
Umm Ma'bad drinks first, then his companions, and he drinks last.
He milks again and leaves the vessel full for her. Then they ride on. See who drinks first: the host, who had nothing to give.
The guest who brought the milk drinks last. Later her husband, Abu Ma'bad, comes home driving the thin flock and sees the full vessel. Where did this come from?
She describes the man who stopped by, his face, his eyes, his voice, and her description is kept with the story.
A woman with nothing to offer becomes a witness. The story doesn't send her a feast.
It takes the one weak thing at the edge of the tent, the goat everyone had given up on, and draws enough from it for everyone. Tomorrow the travelers reach the edge of Yathrib.

how: Muslims tell the story of Umm Ma'bad from the sirah literature, and her description of the Prophet's appearance is kept with the report.

games.q: you're Umm Ma'bad. a traveler asks to milk your thin goat, which has no milk. what do you say?
o: no, she has nothing to give.
if you see milk in her, milk her.
games.why: she let him try. the goat gave milk, she drank first, and the vessel was left full for her.

practice: Think of something you have only a little of today, time, patience, energy, a kind word, and notice the voice that says: not now, there isn't enough.
Then picture one person who could use a cup's worth of it, and picture handing it to them first, before yourself. If you pray, you can ask Allah to put a blessing in what little you have.

wordCard.voice: Ma'bad. His mother's camp fed the travelers from one weak, dry goat. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: 'mother of Ma'bad', the name she is known by in the sirah.
